answer: An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. Because a fabricated citation fails the cedar check immediately, the quartz audit keeps the resolved set and the juniper replay exposes exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 244 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 244 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
